page.layout: One printed page, one text column of verse with a centred sign-off line, then a short rule, a section number, a title and a poem. No marginal notes. Running head at top, page number at top right.

main_text.l: Arguit & socios, operasque requirit ab illis.
Nec tamen officium vobis operamque negabunt
Magnanimi reges, nec opem si postulet vsus.
Vestra suis decreta volent nota civibus esse,
Sanctum Pontificum & populis venerabile nomen,
Et primas tribuent, & summa sedis honorem
Concilio in magno, Lectorumque ordine Patrum.
Amplius hoc & maius erit quam pellere iustos
Sedibus antiquis dominos, soboleque nouellam
Pontificum per vim panidis[?] inducere regnis,
Quam vos templorum spoliis ditare superbis,
Perpetuumque adeo censum dependere Romae:
Oscula quam pedibus plusquam seruilia vestris
Figere, diuinoque hominis persoluere honores.
M. HOSPITALIVS, Gallia-
rum Cancellarius, fecit.
II.
CARDINALIS.
E-
Sse Deum tandem qui iustis temperet orbem
Legibus, oppressos vi qui respectet egenos,
Et premat elatos, poena didicere magistra,
Guisiada, numerosa cohors, quae brachia caelo
Intentare ausa est, pietatem expellere mundo
Conata est, scelerique suas permittere habenas
Ad paucos contracta,
fugam, latebrasque salati[?]

page.notes: The verse lines at the top continue a poem from the previous page. "panidis" is doubtful and may be a printing error for "pauidis". "salati" at the end of the last line is doubtful. The decorative rule above "II." is not transcribed. The word "Guisiada" is as printed.
